verified_contracts: Chinese/English normal and streaming service paths perform collection and explicit confirmation before a real high-priority refund_threshold ticket is created for ORD3001 amount1299.
The ticket retains order, amount, original reason and process_refund audit context; durable assistant metadata and body name the same actual ticket.
Copy explicitly says no refund has been issued; it does not claim an agent picked up or invent a refund receipt.

SQLite trigger refusal yields honest failed handoff with no ticket ID/queue claim; a later order-status tool can run before explicit staff retry without losing the original refund review snapshot or repeating refund execution.
A successful retry retains high priority/refund_threshold; after resolving that ticket a future unrelated staff request is explicit/normal priority.
Active open or claimed tickets are reused; current assignment is preserved, an existing emotion reason stays intact and refund_threshold is retained in escalation_contexts.
Missing handoff service cannot confirm review; ordinary ORD1001 low-value refunds still require confirmation and do not escalate (normal/stream, English yes remains accepted).
An Agent-style staged pending_confirmation contract in the actual checkpointer reaches the same confirmed review path; this is not a test of an LLM Agent selecting that contract.

Two strict JWT HTTP cases stage through the real service, then confirm through /api/v1/chat or /api/v1/chat/stream. Independent SSE decoding sees one complete ticket acknowledgement and persisted text exactly matches visible text.

The manual-review terminal branch clears active slot collections only after saving ticket/retry context; queries for a different same-owner order use the new order ID and foreign-order queries cannot be replaced by the old authorized order.

Abandoning a failed manual review with cancel or no clears its retry meaning; a future ordinary staff request is not classified as an urgent refund escalation. Both normal and streaming service paths are covered.

slot_contamination.observed: After failed refund handoff, querying same-owner ORD3002 or foreign ORD1001 actually executed stale ORD3001 due active filled_slots surviving terminal handoff.
slot_contamination.after: Same-owner ORD3002 is queried with its own args; foreign ORD1001 is refused. Explicit review retry still uses the original ORD3001 refund context, without another refund call.

abandoned_retry_context.after: cancel/no normal/stream produces a later ordinary explicit/normal ticket, with original refund handler still called only once.

limits: No paid/external model, vector service, Redis, production database, deployment or live production probe was used.
All database state is temporary SQLite with foreign keys ON. No claim is made about new PostgreSQL concurrency coverage.
HTTP cases cover successful final confirmation; database-refusal/missing-service/retry failures are tested through actual service normal/stream paths.
The business refund handler remains the documented bundled mock. This iteration verifies durable staff review work, not a real payment integration.
HTTP coverage is limited to final successful confirmation; refusal/retry/cancel/foreign-order cases run through real normal/stream service methods.
The Agent case starts from an Agent-style staged checkpoint contract; it does not measure a live LLM Agent deciding to stage it.
Failed review retry context depends on checkpoint availability and is scoped to the current unsubmitted review in the session. It is not a payment transaction ledger or durable outbox.
Validation used no deployment, production traffic or remote CI. Changes were committed afterwards at the user request; no push.
next_candidates: Shared L0 read eligibility still bypasses applicable user/session context.
Known FAILED-only assistant populations still appear as100% containment under the current no-ticket/no-downvote proxy; additive failure visibility is a separate metric-design iteration.
Live probe remains routing smoke and accepts locally demonstrated failure/unsupported-policy text shapes.
